questions.problem:
The continuous random variable $X$ has the probability density function $f(x)$ stated below. Given that $\text{E}[X]=\frac{11}{12},$ compute $\text{Var}[X].$ Round your answer to $2$ decimal places.

$$
f(x)=\{\begin{aligned}1-{x}^{2}, & 0<x<1, \\ \frac{1}{6}, & 1\le x<3, \\ 0,\, & \text{otherwise.}\end{aligned}
$$
questions.worked_solution:
For a continuous random variable $X$ with probability density function $f(x)$ defined over a set $S,$ we can calculate the variance using the following formula:

$$
\text{Var}[X]=\text{E}[{X}^{2}]-\text{E}[X]^{2}
$$

 

We compute $\text{E}[{X}^{2}],$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{E}[{X}^{2}] & ={\int }_{0}^{3}{x}^{2}\cdot f(x)\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}{x}^{2}\cdot f(x)\,\text{d}x+{\int }_{1}^{3}{x}^{2}\cdot f(x)\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}{x}^{2}\cdot (1-{x}^{2})\,\text{d}x+{\int }_{1}^{3}{x}^{2}\cdot \frac{1}{6}\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}({x}^{2}-{x}^{4})\,\text{d}x+{\int }_{1}^{3}\frac{{x}^{2}}{6}\,\text{d}x \\  & ={(\frac{{x}^{3}}{3}-\frac{{x}^{5}}{5})|}_{0}^{1}+{\frac{{x}^{3}}{18}|}_{1}^{3} \\  & =\frac{71}{45}\end{aligned}
$$

 

Therefore, the variance is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{Var}[X] & =\text{E}[{X}^{2}]-\text{E}[X]^{2} \\  & =\frac{71}{45}-{(\frac{11}{12})}^{2} \\  & ≈0.74\end{aligned}
$$

 
rounded to $2$ decimal places.

questions.problem:
Given that $X$ is a continuous random variable with the following probability density function, compute $\text{Var}[X].$ 

$$
f(x)=\{\begin{aligned}\frac{x}{8},\, & 0\le x\le 4, \\ 0,\, & \text{otherwise.}\end{aligned}
$$
questions.worked_solution:
For a continuous random variable $X$ with probability density function $f(x)$ defined over a set $S,$ we can calculate the variance using the following formula:

$$
\text{Var}[X]=\text{E}[{X}^{2}]-\text{E}[X]^{2}
$$

 

First, we compute $\text{E}[X]:$

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{E}[X] & ={\int }_{0}^{4}x\cdot \frac{x}{8}\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{4}\frac{{x}^{2}}{8}\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\frac{{x}^{3}}{24}|}_{0}^{4} \\  & =\frac{8}{3}\end{aligned}
$$

 

Then, we compute $\text{E}[{X}^{2}]:$

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{E}[{X}^{2}] & ={\int }_{0}^{4}{x}^{2}\cdot \frac{x}{8}\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{4}\frac{{x}^{3}}{8}\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\frac{{x}^{4}}{32}|}_{0}^{4} \\  & =8\end{aligned}
$$

 

Therefore, the variance is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{Var}[X] & =\text{E}[{X}^{2}]-\text{E}[X]^{2} \\  & =8-{(\frac{8}{3})}^{2} \\  & =\frac{8}{9}.\end{aligned}
$$

questions.problem:
The continuous random variable $X$ has the probability density function $f(x)$ stated below. Given that $\text{E}[X]=0.65,$ compute $\text{Var}[X].$ Round your answer to $2$ decimal places.

$$
f(x)=\{\begin{aligned}\frac{4}{5}, & 0<x<1, \\ \frac{1}{{x}^{6}}, & 1\le x, \\ 0,\, & \text{otherwise.}\end{aligned}
$$
questions.worked_solution:
For a continuous random variable $X$ with probability density function $f(x)$ defined over a set $S,$ we can calculate the variance using the following formula:

$$
\text{Var}[X]=\text{E}[{X}^{2}]-\text{E}[X]^{2}
$$

 

We compute $\text{E}[{X}^{2}],$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{E}[{X}^{2}] & ={\int }_{0}^{\infty }{x}^{2}\cdot f(x)\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}{x}^{2}\cdot f(x)\,\text{d}x+{\int }_{1}^{\infty }{x}^{2}\cdot f(x)\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}{x}^{2}\cdot \frac{4}{5}\,\text{d}x+{\int }_{1}^{\infty }{x}^{2}\cdot \frac{1}{{x}^{6}}\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}\frac{4{x}^{2}}{5}\,\text{d}x+{\int }_{1}^{\infty }\frac{1}{{x}^{4}}\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\frac{4{x}^{3}}{15}|}_{0}^{1}+{(-\frac{1}{3{x}^{3}})|}_{1}^{\infty } \\  & =0.6\end{aligned}
$$

 

Therefore, the variance is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{Var}[X] & =\text{E}[{X}^{2}]-\text{E}[X]^{2} \\  & =0.6-(0.65)^{2} \\  & ≈0.18\end{aligned}
$$

 
rounded to $2$ decimal places.

questions.problem:
The continuous random variable $X$ has the probability density function $f(x)$ stated below. Given that $\text{E}[X]=e-1,$ compute $\text{Var}[X].$

$$
f(x)=\{\begin{aligned}\frac{1}{x},\, & 1\le x\le e, \\ 0,\, & \text{otherwise.}\end{aligned}
$$
questions.worked_solution:
For a continuous random variable $X$ with probability density function $f(x)$ defined over a set $S,$ we can calculate the variance using the following formula:

$$
\text{Var}[X]=\text{E}[{X}^{2}]-\text{E}[X]^{2}
$$

 

We compute $\text{E}[{X}^{2}],$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{E}[{X}^{2}] & ={\int }_{1}^{e}{x}^{2}\cdot \frac{1}{x}\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{1}^{e}x\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\frac{{x}^{2}}{2}|}_{1}^{e} \\  & =\frac{{e}^{2}-1}{2}\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the variance is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{Var}[X] & =\text{E}[{X}^{2}]-\text{E}[X]^{2} \\  & =\frac{{e}^{2}-1}{2}-{(e-1)}^{2} \\  & =\frac{4e-{e}^{2}-3}{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

questions.problem:
The continuous random variable $X$ has the probability density function $f(x)$ stated below. Given that $\text{E}[X]=\frac{5}{3},$ compute $\text{Var}[X].$ 

$$
f(x)=\{\begin{aligned}\frac{x}{3}, & 0<x<2 \\ \frac{2(3-x)}{3},\, & 2\le x<3 \\ 0 & \text{otherwise}\end{aligned}
$$
questions.worked_solution:
For a continuous random variable $X$ with probability density function $f(x)$ defined over a set $S,$ we can calculate the variance using the following formula:

$$
\text{Var}[X]=\text{E}[{X}^{2}]-\text{E}[X]^{2}
$$

 

We compute $\text{E}[{X}^{2}],$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{E}[{X}^{2}] & ={\int }_{0}^{3}{x}^{2}\cdot f(x)\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{2}{x}^{2}\cdot f(x)\,\text{d}x+{\int }_{2}^{3}{x}^{2}\cdot f(x)\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{2}{x}^{2}\cdot \frac{x}{3}\,\text{d}x+{\int }_{2}^{3}{x}^{2}\cdot \frac{2(3-x)}{3}\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{2}\frac{{x}^{3}}{3}\,\text{d}x+{\int }_{2}^{3}\frac{6{x}^{2}-2{x}^{3}}{3}\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\frac{{x}^{4}}{12}|}_{0}^{2}+(\frac{2{x}^{3}}{3}-\frac{{x}^{4}}{6}){|}_{2}^{3} \\  & =\frac{4}{3}+(18-\frac{27}{2})-(\frac{16}{3}-\frac{8}{3}) \\  & =\frac{4}{3}+\frac{11}{6} \\  & =\frac{19}{6}\end{aligned}
$$

 

Therefore, the variance is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{Var}[X] & =\text{E}[{X}^{2}]-\text{E}[X]^{2} \\  & =\frac{19}{6}-{(\frac{5}{3})}^{2} \\  & =\frac{7}{18}.\end{aligned}
$$
